questions.question: What does list.append('Item') do?
options: Adds 'Item' to the end of the list
questions.correct_answer: Adds 'Item' to the end of the list
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! .append() pushes an element onto the end of the list.
questions.explanation_incorrect: .append() places the new item at the very end.

questions.question: What does list.pop() with no arguments do?
options: Removes and returns the last item
questions.correct_answer: Removes and returns the last item
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! .pop() removes and returns the trailing element.
questions.explanation_incorrect: .pop() defaults to removing the last element.

questions.question: What is the result of [1, 2, 3, 4, 5][1:3]?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Slicing [1:3] includes index 1 and 2, stopping before 3: [2, 3].
questions.explanation_incorrect: Slicing is start-inclusive and end-exclusive, giving [2, 3].

questions.question: Can a single Python list store mixed data types (e.g. ['Alice', 25, True])?
options: Yes, Python lists can hold any combination of types
No, all elements must be identical types
questions.correct_answer: Yes, Python lists can hold any combination of types
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Python lists are dynamic and heterogeneous.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Python lists can hold mixed data types simultaneously.
